title: Yara and the Harvest
premise: Mara Ashgrove, a nonbinary urban explorer haunted by seven years of rationalized noises, discovers the unmapped tunnels beneath their rented house lead to a subterranean orchard where something ancient still 'harvests' what it is owed. The mirrors' one-second delay reveals that Mara's grandfather took a seed from that place in 1974, and the entity has been patiently collecting his bloodline ever since — including Mara's partner, Dev, who vanishes into the reflection-world mid-story. To survive, Mara must descend, return the seed, and accept that belonging to the orchard means being harvested in turn; they strike a bargain that frees Dev but binds Mara as the new keeper of the frost-patterned gate, ending with them tending the tunnels willingly, no longer able to tell which side of the mirror they stand on.
about_author: Ulyana Ishikawa is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade documenting basements, storm drains, and structures that official maps forgot. Their fiction grows out of that archive of forgotten spaces, blending procedural detail with quiet dread.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. While mapping the house's cellar for their tunnel blog, Mara notices every mirror reflects the room a beat behind — a teacup falls before it shatters in the glass. They film it, measure it, and almost convince themselves it's frame-rate lag. The chapter ends when the reflection raises its hand first. Emotional beat: rationality beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Digging through county archives, Mara finds the 1974 survey shows a tunnel that was sealed and then erased from all later records — signed off by their grandfather, Elias Ashgrove. A neighbor mentions Elias came back from 'the winter job' changed, and never spoke again. Emotional beat: dread shifting from the supernatural to family inheritance.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mara in the present, Elias in 1974 diary fragments. Elias descended during a city project, found an orchard growing without sun, and pocketed a seed he believed was payment. The diary's last entry describes frost forming words on the cellar wall. In the present, Mara finds the seed wrapped in oilcloth. Emotional beat: guilt across generations.

chapters.title: Dev Hears It Too
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, skeptical until now, starts hearing harvesting sounds under the floorboards — shears, wet footsteps, a lullaby hummed by something with too many throats. He defends Mara against their own spiraling doubt, insisting they face it together. The mirrors begin showing a room that isn't theirs: an orchard, bare and waiting. Emotional beat: love as anchor.

chapters.title: Taken Through the Glass
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During a power outage, the mirrors stop delaying and start pulling. Dev reaches for Mara and is drawn into the reflection — Mara watches him walk away inside the glass, unaging, toward the orchard. Emergency services find nothing. The frost writes Dev's name on the cellar wall. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Down Where the Sun Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Armed with the seed and Elias's route, Mara enters the tunnels: brickwork that predates the city, roots grown through concrete like veins, walls furred with frost that spells warnings. They pass older harvest-tokens left by other families who also 'took.' Emotional beat: awe curdling into understanding of scale.

chapters.title: The Orchard of the Owed
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, fraying. In the orchard, trees bear fruit shaped like memories, and Mara sees previous keepers rooted and dreaming, content — including, briefly, a vision of what staying would feel like: warm, belonging, painless. Dev is found alive among the rows, already forgetting Mara's name. Emotional beat: temptation of surrender.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Frost
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. The entity — the Gardener, a figure of woven root and mirror-shard — offers terms: the seed returned buys one life back, but a keeper must hold the gate. Mara negotiates fiercely, refusing to simply trade themselves, forcing the Gardener to honor the original 1974 contract's loophole: a willing keeper chooses freely. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed from horror.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Released through the mirror, Dev wakes in the cellar and fights to go back for Mara, reliving the descent from outside as frost climbs the walls. He witnesses the exchange: Mara pressing the seed into the soil, taking the Gardener's shears. The final pattern completes around Mara's name. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt and helpless witness.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Gate
chapters.summary: Split epilogue-POV. Dev tends the house above, leaving offerings at the cellar door; below, Mara keeps the orchard, half-rooted, no longer certain which side of the mirror is real — but choosing it daily. The last image: a new explorer's flashlight in the tunnels, and Mara stepping forward to greet them, gently. Emotional beat: belonging purchased at terrible cost, worn with strange peace.
